title: RAW complete Justinian II.1.26: former-owner reference survives accession while thief and maker may differ
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_SOURCE_ONLY. Concretizes existing395 with the entire purple-accession paragraph. A fixed historical-owner relation carries the original purple owner through accession into two later claims against its thief; an explicit same/other branch allows the thief to differ from the garment maker. Updating title cannot retarget the claimant, and loss of vindication cannot erase condiction. Eight literal obligation blocks retained, including higher-value purple and the unspecified subset of other possessors. No target, word values, test or decoder.
proposal_kind: Bounded content refinement of existing IDEA000395; not a new source/family and not a rewrite of that card.

design.mechanism: A historical owner-of relation remains bound to the same purple through accession, while current title and distinct remedy/defendant relations are evaluated separately.
design.unit: The entire owned InstitutesII.1.26 paragraph, Si tamen alienam purpuram... through ...quibusdam aliis possessoribus possunt.
design.contrast: Former owner versus overwritten current owner; thief versus necessarily-identical garment maker; condiction surviving versus erased alongside vindication.
design.prediction: Both same-maker and different-thief branches retain the same original-owner claimant and purple reference; changing thief identity changes the defendant, not the accession outcome or claimant.
design.scope: Source-only, unexecuted incomplete Voynich hypothesis; no new legal, historical or manuscript fact.

source.work: Justinian Institutes II.1.26, complete purple-accession paragraph within ownedII.1.25–28
source.text: Si tamen alienam purpuram quis intexuit suo vestimento, licet pretiosior est purpura, accessionis vice cedit vestimento: et qui dominus fuit purpurae, adversus eum qui subripuit habet furti actionem et condictionem, sive ipse est qui vestimentum fecit, sive alius. nam extinctae res licet vindicari non possint, condici tamen a furibus et a quibusdam aliis possessoribus possunt.

full_source_obligations.literal: Si tamen alienam purpuram quis intexuit suo vestimento
full_source_obligations.complete_obligation: A person W weaves another person’s purple P into W’s own garment G. Keep actor-relative foreign/own and both objects; do not assume that garment maker M is necessarily the weaving actor W.
Purple is the more valuable material in this case. Value superiority does not reverse the following accession claim.
Purple follows the garment by accession. This is a historical legal-source assertion, not physical disappearance or a statement of modern law.
The next claimant is the person O who WAS owner of the purple. The historical relation to P survives the changed title description.

full_source_obligations.literal: adversus eum qui subripuit habet furti actionem et condictionem
full_source_obligations.complete_obligation: O has both the theft action and condiction against the person T who stole it. Two remedy kinds, one explicitly typed defendant role, same purple reference.

full_source_obligations.literal: sive ipse est qui vestimentum fecit, sive alius
full_source_obligations.complete_obligation: T may be the garment maker M or someone else. These are alternative identity branches, not two separate claimants or two purple items.

full_source_obligations.literal: nam extinctae res licet vindicari non possint
full_source_obligations.complete_obligation: The explanatory general rule says extinct things cannot be vindicated. Extinct is not silently rendered as destruction of physical material.

full_source_obligations.literal: condici tamen a furibus et a quibusdam aliis possessoribus possunt.
full_source_obligations.complete_obligation: Condiction can nevertheless concern thieves and certain other possessors. The subset of other possessors is not enumerated; do not make all possessors liable.

roles.O: Owner of purple before accession; source qui dominus fuit.
roles.W: Person weaving purple into W’s own garment.
roles.M: Person who made the garment; source garment-maker role.

objects.P: The same purple material, followed across the paragraph.

identity_constraints: O and W are distinct under the actor-relative alienam/suo setup.
T=M or T differs from M are explicitly separate source branches.
Whether M=W is not resolved merely by naming both roles; no extra equality assumed.
No fresh P or O is introduced when title or remedy changes.

multi_statement_chain.content: P belongs to O before W incorporates it into own garmentG. P is more valuable but followsG by accession.
multi_statement_chain.carried_reference: Keep the earlier OWNER_AT(O,P,before) relation; do not overwrite it when describing accession.

multi_statement_chain.content: FORMER_OWNER(P,earlier relation)=O becomes claimant in CLAIM_AGAINST(O,T,P,FURTI_ACTIO) and CLAIM_AGAINST(O,T,P,CONDICTIO).
multi_statement_chain.carried_reference: The P and O of step1 persist; current garment title is not the claimant lookup key.

multi_statement_chain.content: Evaluate the two source role possibilities T=M and T!=M.
multi_statement_chain.new_consequence: O remains claimant and P remains the claim object; only who fills defendantT changes. A maker-only interpretation misses the other-person branch.

multi_statement_chain.content: The explanatory extinct-thing rule blocks vindication while retaining condiction against thieves and a qualified subset of other possessors.
multi_statement_chain.new_consequence: One lost remedy does not delete every claim relation. The unspecified other-possessor subclass remains a source debt, not a universal liability rule.

concrete_competing_whole_bindings.change: Interpret the later owner expression by looking up whoever owns the completed garment/result now.
concrete_competing_whole_bindings.consequence: Can substitute W for O as claimant after accession, despite qui dominus fuit purpurae. Keeps physical objects and apparent source order but changes the historical reference.
Cannot represent sivealius while retaining the same theft/claim relation. No new thief is created per remedy.

concrete_competing_whole_bindings.change: Collapse vindication and condiction into a single recovery-possible flag.
concrete_competing_whole_bindings.consequence: Extinct-thing clause then either removes the expressly retained condiction or preserves the expressly unavailable vindication.

concrete_competing_whole_bindings.change: Treat quibusdam aliis possessoribus as every other holder.
concrete_competing_whole_bindings.consequence: Adds a universality not supplied by the owned paragraph. A complete later truth table cannot use that shortcut.

strongest_known_countercase.source_literal: nam extinctae res licet vindicari non possint, condici tamen a furibus et a quibusdam aliis possessoribus possunt.
strongest_known_countercase.retained_force: Loss of a separate thing/recovery route is not loss of every remedy. The same owned paragraph also explicitly allows a thief other than the maker. These countercases already occur in395’s source; they are not new historical discoveries.
strongest_known_countercase.candidate_limit: The paragraph does not name the eligible other possessors or define all conditions of theft/condiction. A total executable liability classifier would therefore invent law. This proposal stays partial exactly there.
